frequency_question: How often do highly partisan, restrictive voting bills pass the U.S. Senate within a 300-day window when advance signals (such as prior committee hearings, bipartisan backing, or floor scheduling) do not show pre-existing majority support?
membership_rule: Includes major standalone federal election/voter eligibility bills brought to a vote in the Senate from the 116th through 118th Congresses; excludes routine appropriations and non-controversial technical corrections.

skeleton: Legislative sessions with polarizing standalone electoral bills considered in the Senate, categorized by presence or absence of advance consensus signals.
multiplier: 0 hits out of 4 documented comparable partisan major bills without prior consensus signals.
